LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toMeasure_absolut: For probability mass functions p,q on a space with measurable singletons, the measure induced by p is absolutely continuous with respect to the measure induced by q exactly when supp(p) ⊆ supp(q).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_pmf_ne_top_: For finite discrete distributions p,q, D(p∥q) is finite exactly when every outcome with positive p-mass has positive q-mass.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_pmf_eq_top_: For finite discrete laws p,q, D(p∥q) = +∞ exactly when some outcome has positive mass under p and zero mass under q.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_pmf_eq_zero: For probability mass functions p,q on a space with measurable singletons, their extended KL divergence is zero exactly when the two laws are equal.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_pmf_: For finite discrete p,q with supp(p) ⊆ supp(q), their real KL divergence is zero exactly when p=q.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toMeasure_withDen: Let p and q be probability mass functions on a countable space with measurable singletons. If the measure induced by p is absolutely continuous with respect to the measure induced by q, weighting the latter by p(a)/q(a) gives the measure of p. At a point where q(a)=0, absolute continuity forces p(a)=0. Lean gives this 0/0 ratio the value zero, and that point contributes no mass.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_pmf_: For finite discrete laws with p absolutely continuous with respect to q, D(p∥q) = ∑ₐ p(a) ln(p(a)/q(a)) as a real number, with zero contribution from atoms of zero p-mass.
For a finite discrete distribution p supported on a nonempty finite set S, the real KL divergence to the uniform distribution on S equals ln|S| − H(p).
For a law p on a nonempty finite discrete alphabet A, the real KL divergence to the uniform law on A equals ln|A| − H(p).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_eq_toR: For a finite discrete pair law, mutual information is the real KL divergence of its joint law from the independent product of its two marginal probability mass functions.

For finite alphabets with measurable singleton pairs, let P be the joint probability measure of (X,Y) and Q the product of its marginal measures. Then I(X;Y) equals the real value of D(P‖Q), the KL divergence of the joint measure from the product of its marginals.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoFst: Let X and Y take values in finite alphabets with the discrete measurable structure on their product. For Pr[Z=c] > 0, this quantity is the finite KL divergence from the conditional joint law of (X,Y) given Z=c to the product of its two marginals. For Pr[Z=c] = 0, its value is defined to be zero.

Let (X,Y,Z) have a joint probability mass function. Suppose X and Y have finite alphabets and each singleton {(x,y)} is measurable in their product alphabet. For each c with Pr[Z=c] > 0, the fiber mutual information equals the real KL divergence of the conditional joint law of (X,Y) given Z=c from the product of its conditional marginals. When Pr[Z=c] = 0, both scalars are defined to be zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_eq: Let X,Y,Z have finite alphabets and suppose each singleton {(x,y)} is measurable in the pair alphabet. Then I(X;Y|Z) is the weighted sum over c with positive mass of the real KL divergence of the conditional joint law of (X,Y) given Z=c from the product of its two marginals. The weight is Pr[Z=c], and values of zero mass contribute zero.
